what_happened: In job 8gp8 (the disk-space guard retried as a new job), the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The reading was not what the user meant. The user restated the decision from the last critique. Free disk is checked only before dispatch. If space is below the minimum (default 10G in config.rs, no athena.toml edit) after cleaning closed jobs' target/ directories, the job is not dispatched. It stays queued with the reason 'environment: low disk', and status and drain output show the free and required amounts, so nothing mid-run needs resuming. Before the checks, a shortfall must fail fast with a clear environment reason as a retryable failure, not a rejection, instead of holding the job. The user also reminded Athena to write 'the user' and not the word the boundary scan bans.
cause: The reading stage works from the request text alone. This is the same job family as case 374q, a retry of the disk-space guard. The reading did not carry over the decision the last critique settled, so where the check runs and what happens on a shortfall were left open or chosen again. It is also not checked against the repo's current state (the config.rs default) or the boundary word list. Nothing compares a retry's reading with the prior decisions, existing defaults or writing rules before it is accepted. The user is the only carrier of those facts, so the same corrections come back on each attempt.
prevention: Add a pre-acceptance check on every reading. (1) Scan its text against the boundary word list and reject it on a hit. (2) Verify that each config deliverable names a setting without a code default, and that each deliverable is not already landed. (3) For a retry or follow-up, attach the prior attempt's recorded decisions and critique outcomes, and require the reading to state each one or say why it differs. For this class, the check would have forced the reading to carry the settled decision: check only before dispatch, stay queued with the reason, and fail fast before the checks. It would also have caught the banned word and the unneeded config edit.
proposed_request: Add a disk-space guard that checks free disk only before dispatch. First clean closed jobs' target/ directories. If free space is still below the minimum (default 10G from config.rs; make no athena.toml edit), do not dispatch the job. Leave it queued with the reason 'environment: low disk', and show the free and required amounts in `athena status` and in drain output, so nothing mid-run needs resuming. Before the checks run, if free space is below the minimum, fail fast with a clear environment reason as a retryable failure, not a rejection, and do not hold the job. Add tests for the queued case, the amounts shown in status and drain output, and the fail-fast retryable case. Do not change anything already landed in commit 173d12e. Use the words 'the user' and avoid any word the boundary scan bans.
